title: Driver position fanout to rider sockets
name: Trip position fanout

locateQuestion.prompt: Is there a defect in how this fanout manages rider connections and their subscriptions? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
locateQuestion.explanation: The close handler only removes the client from the clients map. Its client id stays in every per-trip subscriber set it joined (client.trips is never used to clean up), and the trip entry stays in subscribers. For trips that never call endTrip (cancelled, abandoned, gateway restarts of the trip service), the sets grow forever, and every publish iterates dead ids. It is a slow memory leak and the stats() subscriptions count drifts upward. Closing should iterate client.trips and call unsubscribe for each.

choiceQuestions.prompt: A rider's phone is on a poor network and its socket has 400 KB queued. A new driver position arrives for its trip. What happens?
choices: The frame is skipped for that rider and the dropped counter increments
The frame is queued anyway and delivered later
publish throws and other riders on the trip miss the update
choiceQuestions.explanation: publish checks bufferedAmount > MAX_BUFFERED_BYTES (256 KB) and, if exceeded, increments dropped and continues. It does not terminate or throw, and the frame is never sent to that socket, so it is not queued.

choiceQuestions.prompt: Why is skipping position frames for a slow socket an acceptable policy for this particular stream?
choices: Because ws guarantees eventual delivery of skipped frames
Because each position supersedes the previous one, so a rider only needs the latest
Because riders resend missed positions on reconnect
Because the trip service retries publish on failure
choiceQuestions.explanation: Driver positions are snapshots: the next frame fully replaces the last, so dropping intermediate ones loses nothing essential and protects server memory. ws does not redeliver skipped frames, riders do not resend anything, and nothing in the code retries publish.

choiceQuestions.prompt: The serialized frame in publish is built once per call rather than once per subscriber. What is the main effect of that under heavy fanout?
choices: It guarantees all riders get identical ordering across trips
It makes publish safe to call concurrently from multiple threads
It avoids repeated JSON serialization, keeping the per-subscriber cost to a send call
It prevents slow sockets from blocking fast ones
choiceQuestions.explanation: JSON.stringify runs once and the same string is sent to every subscriber, so cost per extra rider is just the send. It has nothing to do with ordering across trips, Node has a single JS thread here, and slow sockets are handled by the bufferedAmount check, not serialization.
